title: London's Killer Pea-Souper Fog
hook: Burning coal created yellow toxic fog so thick people walked into rivers.

scenes.text: During the 19th century, millions of domestic fireplaces and industrial factories burned heavy, sulfurous bituminous coal across London.

scenes.text: When weather inversions trapped the soot over the Thames valley, it mixed with river damp to create the notorious 'pea-souper' fog.

scenes.text: The smog was a pungent, yellowish-green blanket of sulfuric acid so thick that pedestrians could not see their own feet or hands.

scenes.text: Street traffic ground to a halt: omnibus drivers had to lead horses on foot holding burning torches, while disoriented walkers fell into canals.

scenes.text: The toxic air choked thousands to death from bronchitis, while soot accumulated so heavily that people blew black soot from their noses for days.
